Portland, OR 97240  

Fax: 503-412-4003 or 866-923-0412  

Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Requested service: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion  
CPT: 22551  
Reference number: POC-6B4F896296-38363  
Denial date: August 19, 2026  

Dear Moda Health Appeal Unit:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for cervical fusion surgery, specifically anterior cervical discectomy and fusion at CPT 22551. The denial states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria.

Please overturn the denial and authorize the requested procedure based on the clinical evidence submitted by my treating surgeon, Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The records establish the following:

- I have had 24 months of progressive neck pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits over 10 weeks, from April 30, 2026, through July 9, 2026. Treatment included cervical traction and postural training. The physical-therapy discharge note documents completion of this course without adequate resolution of the condition.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 14, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief.
- The June 5, 2026 cervical MRI shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged C5-C6 level.
- The symptoms, examination findings, and MRI findings are concordant: the C5-C6 lesion and C6 nerve-root compression correspond to the right-sided pain, numbness, and weakness.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance-use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

These records demonstrate a persistent, progressive, functionally significant cervical radiculopathy caused by documented structural nerve-root compression. They also demonstrate failure of extensive nonsurgical treatment, including supervised physical therapy, prolonged NSAID treatment, and injection therapy. The requested ACDF is directed at the documented C5-C6 pathology and is supported by the treating orthopedic surgeon’s clinical assessment.

The plan has not identified in the denial notice the specific medical-necessity guideline, version, section, or criteria used to evaluate this request. The publicly available Moda materials identify CPT 22551 as a cervical spine-surgery code that may be reviewed through the eviCore musculoskeletal program, but they do not establish which exact criteria were applied to my case. Please provide the complete criteria, guideline name and number, version, effective date, clinical-review rationale, and any documentation deficiencies relied upon in making this determination.

If Moda believes that any specific requirement remains unmet, please identify it precisely and explain which submitted record was considered insufficient. I request a clinical peer-to-peer review with the surgeon and a reconsideration based on the complete clinical record.

Please reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22551. If the denial is upheld, please provide the detailed factual and clinical basis for the decision, the exact policy or guideline applied, all records considered, and information regarding any available external review.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal. This appeal must be received no later than February 15, 2027.

Sincerely,

Avery Grant  
Member ID: W620390523  

Attachments:

- August 19, 2026 adverse benefit determination
- MRI cervical spine report dated June 5, 2026
- Physical-therapy records and discharge note
- Medication and treatment history
- Corticosteroid injection record dated May 14, 2026
- Relevant examination findings
- Orthopedic surgical recommendation from Lindqvist, MD
